Theme

Body, health & movement

infection noun

also infectious, contagious, contagion, infected (wound), get infected

classical

Col. 7.5.6: tum praecipuē ovēs contāgiōne vexentur (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 28.34.4

contāgiō, contāgiōnis f.

noun, third declension

contagion, infection: the passing of a disease by contact

Contact, and so the spreading of a disease from one to another; also of a bad example. Contāgium, contāgiī n. is the same word in verse (contāgia, Verg., Ov.).

Other words

  • suppūrātiō, suppūrātiōnis f. — festering, a gathering of pus: an infected wound

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cels. 2.8 (Lewis & Short); Plin. NH 20.16

    The medical writers’ word; the verb is suppūrō, suppūrāre, to fester (Cato Agr. 157.3).

Examples

  • velut contāgiōne quādam pestiferā īnsānīre

    to rave as if from some pestilent contagionLiv. 28.34.4

  • Vulnus aquā lavā, nē suppūret.

    Wash the cut with water, so that it doesn’t get infected.composed

See also disease, ill, cold, wound.

SourcesLewis & Short: contagio · Lewis & Short: suppuratio · Lewis & Short: suppuro
